label: Game B
nuance_found: none seen in 125 s. The opening is a guided chain (catch a gust, give it to a machine, ride the updraft, push a sail, pick up a bell fragment) where the game tells you the next verb each step and there is one obvious action each time. The 'wake three windmills' goal hints at ordering and gust-carrying puzzles, but I did not reach anything that tested that. Judged only on what was shown.
audio: Soft procedural wind noise and pitched chime chords on every interaction; a wind ambience loop; no melodic music heard in the first two minutes.
furthest_progress: Prologue, rang the morning bell, took Mara's staff, caught and gave a gust to the seed wheel, rode the updraft to the loft (goal 'Wake the three windmills 0/3'), pushed the hanging bridge, picked up bell fragment 1/3 on the small platform. Stuck at about 125 s trying to reach the tail sail behind the Mill of Sails.
used_movement_assist: yes, about 9 times in two runs; the harness hung on the long walks (twice on 'Mill of Sails' and once on 'bridge sail') and was restarted, so the second run was played by direct stick only
control_trouble: Heavy. Fixed, swinging camera plus a stick whose direction changes as the camera re-orients, so I could not steer onto bridge mouths. I wedged on planters and fence ends repeatedly, and jumping off ledges returned a 'little current carries you back' message. From about 55 s to 125 s I made almost no progress. A real thumb would do better, but the game gives no cue about where the walkable path is, which is a clarity cost.
best_moment: Gust cupped into the bell, then released into the copper grille, riding the updraft to the loft and seeing the whole tree open out.
worst_moment: Being wedged against a fence end next to a bridge I could see, with the same carried-back message on each attempt and no hint of the route.
verdict: Gorgeous: a painterly storybook look with a gentle, characterful intro. In the 125 s I saw, though, it plays like a guided tutorial where every step is a context button that does what the line above says. I found no choice and no system feeding another. Navigation on a phone with this camera was a fight even when I knew where to go. I would give it more time only if the later windmill puzzles are the real game, but nothing I saw earned that. This rating rests on a partial, harness-limited session and should be weighted accordingly.
